recent_developments.text: Voltaic Semiconductors announced a partnership with Orbital Networks to build sovereign AI data centers in three countries.
Nimbus Compute unveiled its MX3 accelerator, positioning the chip as a lower-cost alternative to Voltaic's Arc line for large-model training.
Voltaic said the partnership expands its presence in government and telecom markets.
Voltaic announced the Arc 5 accelerator, which it expects to begin shipping to customers in the first half of next year.

market_signals.text: Voltaic Semiconductors remains the market leader, with rivals Nimbus Compute, Helix Silicon and Quanta Forge Labs competing for share.
Voltaic Semiconductors reported data-center revenue of $18.4 billion for fiscal 2025, up from $10.2 billion in fiscal 2024.
Voltaic Semiconductors said the rules could affect about 12 percent of its data-center revenue.
Nimbus Compute reported accelerator revenue of $4.1 billion in 2025, up from $2.3 billion in 2024.
Nimbus Compute said two major cloud customers have committed to deploying MX3 clusters next year.

risks.text: Analysts noted that rising competition from Nimbus Compute and in-house chips at large cloud providers could pressure pricing over time.
Nimbus Compute said its exposure to the restricted regions is limited.
Supply of advanced packaging and high-bandwidth memory remains the main constraint on industry growth.
The company acknowledged that its software ecosystem remains less mature than Voltaic's, which remains a barrier to adoption for some customers.
Management warned that limited advanced packaging capacity would remain a supply constraint for at least two more quarters.
